mainTopic: The מעמד's Torah readings, the special wood-offering days, and the stories and families behind them
overview: The amud opens with the last words of an earlier discussion about splitting a short Torah paragraph between readers. Next the גמרא asks how to read the משנה about the אנשי מעמד: was the מוסף reading done from a ספר תורה or by heart? A ברייתא shows that שחרית and מוסף were read from the scroll and only מנחה was by heart. רבי יוסי adds that at מנחה everyone said it together, like שמע. The גמרא then explains that a קרבן מוסף day cancels more of the מעמד than a קרבן עצים day, because the first comes from the Torah and the second is rabbinic. A ברייתא tells how the wood-offering days began: families donated wood when the returning exiles found none, and the נביאים made those days permanent. Two stories explain odd family names. One family hid בכורים under dried figs and carried a pestle past the guards. The other, בני סלמאי, disguised their wood as ladders. The גמרא then identifies the families of פחת מואב and עדין and asks which תנא the משנה follows, answering that it fits one version of רבי יוסי's view. The amud ends as מר קשישא begins a question to רב אשי about the first of טבת, and the question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The second reader has room to continue
steps.stepSummary: The closing words of the previous discussion: the second reader has extra space, because he can continue into the next paragraph.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because he has room.
steps.whatsHappening: These are the last words of the explanation from the previous page. It explains why the second reader is not stuck: he can keep reading into the next paragraph.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier discussion was about splitting a short paragraph among readers. The point here is that the second reader has some extra room, since he may go on into the following paragraph. With this the earlier topic is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: Room, space, leeway
He has

phrases.english: since he has room.
phrases.notes: He means the second reader, who can keep going into the next paragraph.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִית לֵיהּ רַוְוחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an answer that began on the previous daf.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The second reader has room, since he may continue into the following paragraph.

steps.title: The משנה about reading a long passage
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a long passage is read by two people at שחרית and מוסף, and at מנחה it is read by heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: A long passage is read by two people, at the morning prayer and the additional prayer. And at the afternoon prayer they read by heart, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה about the reading of the אנשי מעמד. It is setting up a question about how this line should be read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's wording is unclear. It does not say plainly whether the words 'by heart' apply only to מנחה, or to מוסף as well. The next step asks about exactly this.

keyTerms.meaning: A long Torah paragraph
The morning prayer
The additional prayer
The afternoon prayer
By heart, from memory

phrases.english: A long passage is read by two people
at the morning prayer and the additional prayer.
And at the afternoon prayer they read by heart, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּרָשָׁה גְּדוֹלָה קוֹרִין אוֹתָהּ בִּשְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A long passage is split between two readers; at מנחה it is read by heart.

steps.title: Was מוסף read from the scroll or by heart?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which way to read the משנה: is only מנחה done by heart, or are both מוסף and מנחה done by heart?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: what is the משנה saying? Does it mean that at שחרית and מוסף they read from the scroll, and at מנחה they read by heart like קריאת שמע? Or does it mean that at שחרית they read from the scroll, and at מוסף and מנחה they read by heart like קריאת שמע?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a real question about how the משנה is worded. It lays out two possible ways to read it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is where the words 'by heart' begin in the משנה. Reading 1 groups מוסף with שחרית, so both are from the scroll. Reading 2 groups מוסף with מנחה, so both are by heart.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked (a real question that needs an answer)
How is it saying this? / What does it mean?
From the ספר תורה
Like saying שמע, from memory
Or perhaps

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody is asking about שחרית or מנחה, since everyone agrees on those. The only open question is מוסף: scroll or by heart?

phrases.english: They asked: how is it saying this?
At the morning prayer and the additional prayer they read it from the scroll,

phrases.aramaic: וּבַמִּנְחָה קוֹרִין אוֹתָהּ עַל פֶּה כְּקוֹרִין אֶת שְׁמַע,
phrases.english: and at the afternoon prayer they read it by heart, the way one says שמע,
or perhaps this is what it teaches:
at the morning prayer they read it from the scroll,
and at the additional prayer and the afternoon prayer they read it
by heart, the way one says שמע?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: הֵיכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to read the משנה line just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'by heart' in the משנה include מוסף, or only מנחה?

steps.title: A ברייתא: שחרית and מוסף from the scroll
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying that at שחרית and מוסף they read the normal way, and only at מנחה was it read by heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as a ברייתא teaches: at שחרית and מוסף they go into the בית הכנסת and read the way they read all year. At מנחה, one person reads it by heart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to answer the question. It says that מוסף was read from the scroll, just like שחרית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading 'the way they read all year' means reading from a ספר תורה. Since the ברייתא puts מוסף together with שחרית, the first way of reading the משנה is correct. Only מנחה was by heart.

keyTerms.meaning: The normal way, from a ספר תורה
A single individual

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught:
At the morning prayer and the additional prayer they enter the synagogue
and read the way they read all year,

phrases.aramaic: וּבַמִּנְחָה יָחִיד קוֹרֵא אוֹתָהּ עַל פֶּה.
phrases.english: and at the afternoon prayer one person reads it by heart.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 3 by bringing a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The first reading of the משנה: מוסף was read from the scroll.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that puts מוסף together with שחרית as a normal reading.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: everyone reads together by heart
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי objects that one person may not read Torah by heart for the public. Instead, everyone says it together, like שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: can one person read Torah words by heart in front of the public? Rather, everyone goes in and reads it by heart, like saying שמע.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the same ברייתא, רבי יוסי argues with the first opinion about how the מנחה reading was done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי argues only about who reads at מנחה: everyone together, not one person. He does not argue about מוסף. So both opinions agree that only מנחה was by heart, and the question from step 3 is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: But can...? (a challenging question)
Words of the Written Torah said from memory
In front of the public
All of them, everyone together

steps.whatToRemember: Both opinions in the ברייתא agree: at שחרית and מוסף the reading was from a ספר תורה, and only מנחה was by heart. They argue only about whether one person read at מנחה or everyone together.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
But can a single person read
words of Torah by heart in public?
Rather, they all go in

phrases.aramaic: וְקוֹרִין אוֹתָהּ עַל פֶּה כְּקוֹרִין אֶת שְׁמַע.
phrases.english: and read it by heart, the way one says שמע.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: וְכִי יָחִיד יָכוֹל לִקְרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוסי argues with the first opinion in the ברייתא about the מנחה reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first opinion's claim that one person reads by heart at מנחה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One person may not read Torah words by heart for the public, so the reading must be done by everyone together.

steps.title: The משנה: days with הלל have no מעמד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: on a day with הלל there is no מעמד reading, and it goes on to days with a קרבן מוסף and a קרבן עצים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Any day that has הלל has no מעמד, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה about special days that cancel some of the מעמד's gatherings. It is setting up a question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full משנה lists a ladder of days: a day with הלל cancels the morning gathering, a day with a קרבן מוסף cancels a later one, and a day with a קרבן עצים cancels only the closing prayer. The 'and so on' points to that full list.

keyTerms.meaning: Songs of praise said on holidays
The non-כהן group that gathered to pray and read about בריאה
And so on (the quote continues)

phrases.english: Any day that has הלל
has no מעמד, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל יוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ הַלֵּל אֵין בּוֹ מַעֲמָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Special days cancel some of the מעמד's gatherings, depending on how important the day is.

steps.title: Why the two days are treated differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a day with a קרבן מוסף cancels more than a day with a קרבן עצים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between this one and that one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה treats the קרבן מוסף day and the קרבן עצים day differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both days have a special קרבן. So why does the מוסף day cancel the מנחה gathering, while the עצים day cancels only the closing prayer (נעילה)?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference?
Between this one and that one

phrases.english: What is the difference between this and that?
phrases.notes: He means the day with a קרבן מוסף and the day with a קרבן עצים.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה הֶפְרֵשׁ בֵּין זֶה לָזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does a קרבן מוסף day cancel more of the מעמד than a קרבן עצים day?

steps.title: Torah law versus rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: The קרבן מוסף days come from the Torah, but the קרבן עצים days are rabbinic. So the מוסף days cancel more.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are Torah law, and these are rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the difference comes from where each day's importance comes from: the Torah or the Rabbis.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן מוסף day is set by the Torah, so it is stronger and cancels the earlier מנחה gathering. A קרבן עצים day is only rabbinic, so it cancels just the last gathering, נעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: These
Torah law
Rabbinic law

steps.whatToRemember: A day whose importance comes from the Torah cancels more of the מעמד's gatherings than a day whose importance is rabbinic.

phrases.english: These are Torah law,
phrases.notes: These are the days with a קרבן מוסף.

phrases.english: and these are rabbinic law.
phrases.notes: These are the days with a קרבן עצים.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַלָּלוּ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְהַלָּלוּ דִּבְרֵי סוֹפְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The קרבן מוסף comes from the Torah, while the קרבן עצים is rabbinic, so the stronger day cancels more.

steps.title: Why did the משנה need to list the wood-offering days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words about the times for the wood of the כהנים and the people. It then brings a ברייתא that asks why these special days had to be listed at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'The times for the wood of the כהנים and the people, etc.' The רבנן taught: Why did they need to list the times for the wood of the כהנים and the people?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks why these wood days were set up at all. This is setting up the story in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מזבח always needed wood, and the Temple storeroom normally supplied it. So why would particular families have their own fixed days to bring wood? The question asks for the history behind these days.

keyTerms.meaning: The set times when certain families of כהנים and ordinary Jews brought wood for the מזבח
They needed to

phrases.english: The times of the wood of the priests and the people, etc.
The Rabbis taught:
Why did they need to state
the times of the wood of the priests and the people?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: לָמָּה הוּצְרְכוּ לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from explaining why מוסף days cancel more than עצים days. It now asks about the origin of the עצים days themselves.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The historical reason that specific families had fixed days to donate wood.

steps.title: The returning exiles found no wood, so these families donated
steps.stepSummary: When the exiles came back to build the second בית המקדש, the storeroom had no wood. These families stepped forward and gave wood from their own property.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: When the exiles came up to ירושלים, they found no wood in the storeroom. These families got up and donated wood from their own property.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question with a piece of history. These families earned their special days because they gave wood when none was available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The days are not random. They honor the specific families who saved the קרבנות when the storeroom was empty at the start of the second בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: The people of the exile, meaning the Jews who came back from בבל
A chamber in the בית המקדש, here the wood storeroom
They donated willingly

phrases.english: They said: When the people of the exile went up
they did not find wood in the chamber,
and these families arose
and donated from their own.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ: כְּשֶׁעָלוּ בְּנֵי הַגּוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The families donated wood when the returning exiles found the storeroom empty.

steps.title: The נביאים made the donation days permanent
steps.stepSummary: The נביאים of that generation ruled that these families would keep donating their own wood on their days, even when the storeroom was full.
steps.simpleTranslation: The נביאים among them made this condition: even if the storeroom is full of wood, these families will still donate from their own.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its answer. It explains why the days continued even after the shortage ended.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 explains how the days began. This step explains why they lasted: a ruling of the נביאים turned a one-time act into a lasting privilege. That is why the משנה still lists them.

keyTerms.meaning: They made a condition, or set up a rule
Prophets, here the נביאים of the early second בית המקדש period
Full

steps.confusionAlert: The families did not keep bringing wood because the מזבח needed it. They kept bringing it because the נביאים ruled that their days would last forever as an honor.

phrases.english: And so the prophets among them stipulated:
that even if the chamber is full of wood,
these families will donate from their own,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכָךְ הִתְנוּ נְבִיאִים שֶׁבֵּינֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to step 10's history by explaining why the days became permanent.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ruling by the נביאים made the families' donation days permanent, even when wood was plentiful.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why the משנה treats these days as real days of celebration for these families, even generations later.

steps.title: A פסוק in נחמיה supports the fixed wood times
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings a פסוק from נחמיה. It describes lots being cast for the wood offering at set times each year.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'We cast lots for the wood offering, the כהנים, the לוים and the people, to bring it to the house of our God by our fathers' houses, at set times year by year, to burn on the מזבח of ה' our God, as it is written in the Torah.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא backs up the ruling of the נביאים with a פסוק. It shows that the wood offering was organized by family and at fixed times every year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'by our fathers' houses' match the idea that specific families held these days. 'At set times year by year' matches the idea that the days repeat every year forever.

keyTerms.meaning: Lots, used to decide who gets which turn
The wood offering
Set, appointed times
To burn

steps.whatToRemember: The wood days began because these families gave wood when there was none. The נביאים then made the days permanent, and the פסוק in נחמיה shows they were fixed by family, year after year.

phrases.english: as it is stated:
"And we cast lots for the wood offering,
the priests, the Levites, and the people,
to bring it to the house of our God, by our fathers' houses,
at appointed times, year by year,
to burn upon the altar of the Lord our God,
as it is written in the Torah."

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וְהַגּוֹרָלוֹת הִפַּלְנוּ עַל קֻרְבַּן הָעֵצִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק as support for the ruling of the נביאים in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That the wood offering was set by families at fixed times each year.

steps.title: Who were 'בני גונבי עלי' and 'בני קוצעי קציעות'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words about the group that brought wood with the family of זתוא בן יהודה. A ברייתא asks who the families with the strange names were.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And with them were כהנים and לוים and anyone who, etc.' The רבנן taught: Who were the descendants of the pestle-thieves and the descendants of the fig-packers?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another line of the משנה and asks what two odd family names mean. This sets up a story in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists 'בני גונבי עלי' and 'בני קוצעי קציעות' among the wood donors. These names sound strange and even insulting, so the ברייתא asks where they come from.

keyTerms.meaning: The descendants of those who 'stole' with a pestle, meaning they fooled the guards using a pestle
The descendants of those who packed dried figs
A pestle, a heavy tool for pounding

phrases.aramaic: וְעִמָּהֶם כֹּהֲנִים וּלְוִיִּם וְכׇל מִי כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: And with them were priests and Levites and anyone who, etc.
The Rabbis taught:
Who were the descendants of the pestle-deceivers
phrases.notes: Literally 'pestle-thieves'. Here 'stealing' means tricking someone, which the story will explain.

phrases.english: and the descendants of the packers of dried figs?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מָה הָיוּ בְּנֵי גּוֹנְבֵי עֱלִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of why the wood days exist and asks about the names of two families in the משנה's list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning and history behind the names 'בני גונבי עלי' and 'בני קוצעי קציעות'.

steps.title: The wicked kingdom's decree and the roadblocks
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins its answer with a story. A wicked kingdom banned bringing wood for the מזבח and בכורים to ירושלים, and set guards on the roads, just as ירבעם בן נבט did.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Once the wicked kingdom made a decree of persecution against the Jews: they may not bring wood for the מזבח, and they may not bring בכורים to ירושלים. They put guards on the roads, the same way ירבעם בן נבט put guards so that the Jews could not go up for the רגל.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts to answer the question by setting the scene of a persecution. The story of how the families got past the guards comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The background explains the danger. Bringing wood or בכורים had been outlawed and the roads were guarded, so anyone who brought them took a real risk. That courage is what the families' strange names will honor.

keyTerms.meaning: The wicked kingdom, the ruling enemy power
A decree meant to force Jews to give up their religion
The arrangement of wood on the מזבח
First fruits brought to the בית המקדש
Guards or checkpoints on the roads

phrases.english: They said: Once,

phrases.aramaic: גָּזְרָה מַלְכוּת הָרְשָׁעָה שְׁמָד עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: the wicked kingdom decreed persecution against Israel
that they should not bring wood for the altar arrangement,
and that they should not bring first fruits to Jerusalem,
and they placed guards on the roads
the way Jeroboam son of Nevat placed guards,
so that Israel would not go up for the Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ: פַּעַם אַחַת גָּזְרָה מַלְכוּת הָרְשָׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to step 13 by telling the background of the persecution.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer starts with the background: a decree banned bringing wood and בכורים, and guards were posted on the roads. The rest of the story continues after this.

steps.title: Hiding the first fruits under dried figs
steps.stepSummary: The righteous people of that generation hid their בכורים under dried figs and carried a pestle. They told the guards they were going to make fig cakes, then brought the בכורים to ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did the worthy, sin-fearing people of that generation do? They covered their baskets of first fruits with dried figs and carried a pestle on their shoulders. When the guards asked where they were going, they said they were going to make fig cakes with a mortar down the road and the pestle they were carrying. Once they got past the guards, they decorated the baskets and brought them to ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues the story from the last step. It tells how righteous people tricked the guards so they could still bring בכורים to ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The guards were watching for anyone bringing offerings to ירושלים. The dried figs on top and the pestle made the trip look like ordinary farm work. The details of the story (dried figs and a pestle) seem to match the unusual family names listed in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: People who fear sin; very careful, God-fearing people
Baskets of first fruits brought to the בית המקדש
Dried figs
A pestle, the tool used to crush or pound food
Guards posted on the roads
Round cakes of pressed figs

phrases.aramaic: מָה עָשׂוּ כְּשֵׁרִין וְיִרְאֵי חֵטְא שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ הַדּוֹר?
phrases.english: What did the worthy and sin-fearing people of that generation do?
They brought baskets of first fruits
and covered them with dried figs, and took them,
with a pestle on their shoulders.
And when they reached the guards,
the guards said to them: Where are you going?
They said to them:
To make two round cakes of pressed figs
with the mortar that is ahead of us,
and with the pestle that is on our shoulders.
As soon as they passed the guards,
they decorated the baskets and brought them to Jerusalem.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה עָשׂוּ כְּשֵׁרִין וְיִרְאֵי חֵטְא שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ הַדּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun in step 14 by telling how the righteous got around the ban.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who were the families with the strange names in the משנה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They were the brave people who hid their בכורים under dried figs and carried a pestle to fool the guards.

steps.title: These were the descendants of סלמאי הנתופתי
steps.stepSummary: A תנא teaches that the בני סלמאי הנתופתי did something similar.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Sage taught: These were the descendants of סלמאי of נטופה.
steps.whatsHappening: A short teaching links the brave act just described to another family, בני סלמאי הנתופתי. It sets up the next ברייתא, which explains that name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only names the family. It does not yet tell us what they did. The גמרא will now bring a ברייתא to fill in their story.

keyTerms.meaning: A Sage taught (introduces a teaching from the time of the משנה)
The descendants of סלמאי from the town of נטופה

phrases.english: A Sage taught:
These were the descendants of Salmai of Netophat.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: הֵן הֵן בְּנֵי סַלְמַאי הַנְּתוֹפָתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links the first story to another family name, בני סלמאי הנתופתי, which the next ברייתא explains.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בני סלמאי הנתופתי were also among these brave donor families.

steps.title: Who were בני סלמאי הנתופתי?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks who the בני סלמאי הנתופתי were.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Who were the descendants of סלמאי of נטופה?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks to explain this family's name. The answer comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the reason for the name. The answer will be a story that explains it.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Who are the descendants of Salmai of Netophat?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מָה הֵן בְּנֵי סַלְמַאי הַנְּתוֹפָתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the explanation behind the name given in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the story behind the name בני סלמאי הנתופתי?

steps.title: A ban on bringing wood for the מזבח
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins its answer: a wicked kingdom banned bringing wood for the מזבח and put guards on the roads, just like ירבעם בן נבט did.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: Once the wicked kingdom made a decree against the Jews that they could not bring wood for the altar fire. They placed guards on the roads, the same way ירבעם בן נבט placed guards on the roads so that the Jews would not go up for the festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts answering the question by setting the scene. It describes the ban that the next step's story is about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story is similar to the one in step 14, but here the ban is only on wood for the מזבח. The comparison to ירבעם shows how bad this was: guards were used to stop Jews from serving in the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: The wicked kingdom (the foreign rulers)
A decree meant to force Jews to give up their religion
The arranged wood fire on the מזבח
For the festival (going up to ירושלים on the three festivals)

phrases.english: They said: Once,

phrases.aramaic: גָּזְרָה מַלְכוּת הָרְשָׁעָה שְׁמָד עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: the wicked kingdom made a religious decree against the Jews
that they may not bring wood for the altar fire,
and they placed guards on the roads

phrases.aramaic: כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁהוֹשִׁיב יָרׇבְעָם בֶּן נְבָט עַל הַדְּרָכִים,
phrases.english: the same way that Jeroboam son of Nevat placed guards on the roads,
so that the Jews would not go up for the festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ: פַּעַם אַחַת גָּזְרָה מַלְכוּת הָרְשָׁעָה שְׁמָד עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to step 17 by describing the background of the story.
steps.confusionAlert: This sounds like step 14, but it is a separate story. Step 14 led to the fig-and-pestle story; this one is about wood only and leads to the ladder story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The story starts with a ban on bringing wood for the מזבח, enforced by guards on the roads.

steps.title: Carrying the wood as ladders
steps.stepSummary: The sin-fearing people made their wood into ladders, told the guards they were going to fetch young doves, then took the ladders apart and brought the wood to ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did the sin-fearing people of that generation do? They took their logs and made ladders, put them on their shoulders, and went. When they reached the guards, the guards asked where they were going. They said: To bring young doves from the dovecote ahead of us, with these ladders on our shoulders. As soon as they passed the guards, they took the ladders apart and brought the wood up to ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its answer with the clever trick these people used. This explains the family name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ladder looks like an ordinary tool for reaching a dovecote, so the guards let them pass. After the guards, the ladders went back to being wood for the מזבח. The name סלמאי sounds like סולם (ladder), so the name remembers this act.

keyTerms.meaning: Cut pieces of wood, logs
Ladders
Young doves or pigeons
A dovecote, a house where doves nest

steps.whatToRemember: The name סלמאי comes from סולם, ladder. These families risked danger to bring wood to the מזבח by hiding it as ladders.

phrases.aramaic: מָה עָשׂוּ יִרְאֵי חֵטְא שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ הַדּוֹר?
phrases.english: What did the sin-fearing people of that generation do?
They brought their pieces of wood and made ladders,
and put them on their shoulders and went on their way.
When they reached the guards,
the guards said to them: Where are you going?
They said to them:
To bring down young doves from the dovecote ahead of us
with the ladders that are on our shoulders.
phrases.notes: Listen for the wordplay: סולם (ladder) sounds like the family name סלמאי.

phrases.english: As soon as they passed the guards,
they took the ladders apart, brought them, and carried them up to Jerusalem.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה עָשׂוּ יִרְאֵי חֵטְא שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ הַדּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer begun in step 18 with the trick that gave the family its name.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בני סלמאי were those who carried wood for the מזבח disguised as ladders (סולמות).

steps.title: The memory of the righteous is a blessing
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with a פסוק: the righteous, like these families, are remembered for blessing, while the name of ירבעם and those like him will rot.
steps.simpleTranslation: About them and people like them the פסוק says: 'The memory of the righteous is for a blessing.' And about ירבעם בן נבט and his companions it says: 'But the name of the wicked shall rot.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes the stories with one פסוק that praises the brave families and condemns ירבעם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two halves of the same פסוק match the two sides of the story. The families who risked themselves for the מזבח are remembered by name forever. ירבעם, who blocked the roads to the בית המקדש, is remembered only for shame.

keyTerms.meaning: The memory of the righteous is for a blessing
But the name of the wicked shall rot
The king who split off the northern kingdom and stopped people from going to ירושלים

steps.whatToRemember: These family names in the משנה are badges of honor. They remember people who risked danger to keep the מזבח going, while ירבעם's name is a warning.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why the משנה lists these families with their odd names: the names keep their good deeds alive.

phrases.aramaic: וַעֲלֵיהֶם וְעַל כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהֶם הוּא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: And about them and those like them the verse says:
“The memory of the righteous shall be for a blessing,”

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל יָרׇבְעָם בֶּן נְבָט וַחֲבֵרָיו נֶאֱמַר:
phrases.english: and about Jeroboam son of Nevat and his companions it is said:
“But the name of the wicked shall rot.”
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the same פסוק, משלי 10:7.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַעֲלֵיהֶם וְעַל כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהֶם הוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the stories with a פסוק that sums up their message.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The righteous donor families are remembered for blessing, while ירבעם and those like him are remembered for shame.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: בני פחת מואב are the family of דוד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's entry for the twentieth of אב. It brings a ברייתא where רבי מאיר identifies בני פחת מואב בן יהודה as the descendants of דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the twentieth of אב, the family of פחת מואב בן יהודה brought wood. A תנא taught: this family is the same as the family of דוד בן יהודה. That is what רבי מאיר says.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next date in the משנה's list. It explains who this family really is, according to רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name "פחת מואב" sounds unfamiliar. רבי מאיר says it is really just another name for דוד's family. This identification sets up the difficulty that comes later.

keyTerms.meaning: the name of a family listed in the משנה
they are the very same ones

phrases.english: On the twentieth of it
phrases.notes: "It" means the month of אב, which the משנה was just talking about.

phrases.english: the descendants of Pahath Moab ben Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: בְּנֵי פַּחַת מוֹאָב בֶּן יְהוּדָה —
phrases.english: A tanna taught: The descendants of Pahath Moab ben Yehuda —

phrases.aramaic: הֵן הֵן בְּנֵי דָוִד בֶּן יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: they are the very same as the descendants of David ben Yehuda,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: בְּנֵי פַּחַת מוֹאָב בֶּן יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story of בני סלמאי to the next date in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, בני פחת מואב are the descendants of דוד.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: they are the family of יואב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees. He says בני פחת מואב are the descendants of יואב בן צרויה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: they are the family of יואב בן צרויה.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא gives a different answer about who בני פחת מואב are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that פחת מואב is another name for a known family. They only argue about which family it is: דוד or יואב.

keyTerms.meaning: יואב, son of צרויה, the general of דוד's army

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: הֵן הֵן בְּנֵי יוֹאָב בֶּן צְרוּיָה.
phrases.english: they are the very same as the descendants of Joab, son of Zeruiah.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing view to רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, בני פחת מואב are the descendants of יואב בן צרויה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: בני עדין are the family of דוד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's entry for the twentieth of אלול. A ברייתא brings רבי יהודה's view that בני עדין בן יהודה are the descendants of דוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the twentieth of אלול, the family of עדין בן יהודה brought wood. The רבנן taught: this family is the same as the family of דוד בן יהודה. That is what רבי יהודה says.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes to the next date in the משנה and identifies this family too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works just like the last pair of steps. Now it is רבי יהודה who says a different-sounding family name, עדין, really means דוד's family.

keyTerms.meaning: the name of another family in the משנה's list
"etc."; the rest of the line in the משנה

phrases.english: On the twentieth of Elul
the descendants of Adin ben Yehuda, etc.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּנֵי עָדִין בֶּן יְהוּדָה —
phrases.english: The Sages taught: The descendants of Adin ben Yehuda —

phrases.aramaic: הֵן הֵן בְּנֵי דָוִד בֶּן יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: they are the very same as the descendants of David ben Yehuda,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בְּנֵי עָדִין בֶּן יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of identification, now for the next date in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, בני עדין are the descendants of דוד.

steps.title: רבי יוסי again says יואב's family
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says בני עדין are also the descendants of יואב בן צרויה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: they are the family of יואב בן צרויה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי gives the same answer he gave before. He says בני עדין are יואב's family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Put רבי יוסי's two statements together. Both פחת מואב and עדין are יואב's family. That means יואב's family appears on the list two times.
steps.confusionAlert: Keep track of who says what. רבי מאיר speaks about פחת מואב, and רבי יהודה speaks about עדין. Each of them says it is דוד's family. רבי יוסי says יואב's family both times.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: הֵן הֵן בְּנֵי יוֹאָב בֶּן צְרוּיָה.
phrases.english: they are the very same as the descendants of Joab, son of Zeruiah.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing view to רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, בני עדין are also the descendants of יואב.

steps.title: Whose view does the משנה follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that בני פרעוש came a second time on the first of טבת. It asks which תנא wrote this משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the first of טבת, בני פרעוש came back a second time. Who is the author of our משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a problem. The משנה marks only בני פרעוש as coming "a second time," so the גמרא asks whose view that fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the word "second" only for בני פרעוש. This suggests that no other family appears on the list twice. That needs checking against the views just quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: they returned / came again
a second time
whose view is our משנה?

phrases.english: On the first of Tevet
the descendants of Parosh returned a second time, etc.
Who is the author of our mishna?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי מַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the identifications from the last few steps to test the משנה's wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view the משנה's wording, with only בני פרעוש coming a second time, follows.

steps.title: It fits none of the three תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the משנה does not match רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה, or רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not רבי מאיר, not רבי יהודה, and not רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question with a problem: none of the three opinions fits the משנה. The next steps explain why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real difficulty, not just a reply. Each of these תנאים has some family appearing twice, besides בני פרעוש, and the משנה never says so.

keyTerms.meaning: not

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, וְלָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: It is not Rabbi Meir, and not Rabbi Yehuda,
and not Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר, וְלָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְלָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25 by pointing out a difficulty.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's wording, which calls only בני פרעוש a "second time" family.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under each of the three views, another family also appears twice. So the משנה should have said that family came a second time too.

steps.title: Why it can't be רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה followed רבי מאיר, it should have said בני דוד came a second time on the twentieth of אב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were רבי מאיר, the משנה should have said: the family of דוד בן יהודה came back a second time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why רבי מאיר's view does not fit the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already lists בני דוד בן יהודה on an earlier date. רבי מאיר says פחת מואב, on the twentieth of אב, is also דוד's family. So that should have been described as דוד's family coming "a second time."

keyTerms.meaning: if
let him teach / it should have said

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Meir, let him teach:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁבוּ בְּנֵי דָוִד בֶּן יְהוּדָה שְׁנִיָּה!
phrases.english: the descendants of David ben Yehuda returned a second time!
phrases.notes: This would go on the twentieth of אב, the date of בני פחת מואב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי מֵאִיר, לִיתְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the first part of the claim in step 26.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה is not רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי מאיר's statement that פחת מואב is דוד's family.

steps.title: Why it can't be רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה followed רבי יהודה, it should have said בני דוד came a second time on the twentieth of אלול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were רבי יהודה, the משנה should have said: the family of דוד בן יהודה came back a second time!
steps.whatsHappening: Using the same reasoning, the גמרא shows that רבי יהודה's view does not fit either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says עדין, on the twentieth of אלול, is דוד's family. So under his view, דוד's family appears twice on the list. The משנה should have noted that.

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Yehuda, let him teach:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁבוּ בְּנֵי דָוִד בֶּן יְהוּדָה שְׁנִיָּה!
phrases.english: the descendants of David ben Yehuda returned a second time!
phrases.notes: This time it would go on the twentieth of אלול, the date of בני עדין.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, לִיתְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the second part of the claim in step 26.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה is not רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's statement that עדין is דוד's family.

steps.title: Why it can't be רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה followed רבי יוסי, it should have said בני יואב בן צרויה came a second time.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were רבי יוסי, the משנה should have said: the family of יואב בן צרויה came back a second time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof by showing that רבי יוסי's view does not fit the משנה either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says both פחת מואב and עדין are יואב's family. So under his view, יואב's family appears twice. The משנה should have said so, and it doesn't.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה says "a second time" only about בני פרעוש. Under רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, דוד's family would appear twice. Under רבי יוסי, יואב's family would appear twice. So the משנה matches none of them.

phrases.english: If it is Rabbi Yosei, let him teach:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁבוּ בְּנֵי יוֹאָב בֶּן צְרוּיָה שְׁנִיָּה!
phrases.english: the descendants of Joab, son of Zeruiah, returned a second time!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי, לִיתְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the third part of the claim in step 26.

steps.title: The משנה Follows רבי יוסי After All
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה really does follow רבי יוסי. Two תנאים report רבי יוסי's opinion differently, and the משנה matches one of those versions.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the משנה follows רבי יוסי. There are two תנאים who disagree about what רבי יוסי held.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from steps 26–29. It says the משנה does follow רבי יוסי, because there are two different reports of what רבי יוסי held.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge was this: according to רבי יוסי, the משנה should have listed בני יואב בן צרויה a second time. The answer is that two תנאים disagree about which family רבי יוסי counted as בני יואב. One says it is only בני פחת מואב, and the other says it is only בני עדין בן יהודה. On either view, יואב's family was not repeated a second time, so the משנה fits רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually. It signals a return to the original idea, which the גמרא now defends.
Two תנאים, two early teachers who disagree
According to, or in the view of

steps.whatToRemember: When a משנה seems not to fit any known opinion, the גמרא may answer that two תנאים reported one Sage's view differently. The משנה then follows one of those reports.
steps.confusionAlert: The two תנאים are not arguing against רבי יוסי. Both agree with him. They only disagree about exactly what his opinion was.

phrases.english: Actually, it is Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.english: and there are two tannaim with differing versions of Rabbi Yosei's view.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting one Sage's opinion into two reported versions (תרי תנאי אליבא ד...)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי יוסי had one fixed view, which required בני יואב to appear a second time.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two תנאים report רבי יוסי's view differently. In the version the משנה follows, יואב's family was not repeated, so the משנה fits רבי יוסי.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה About the First of טבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that on the first of טבת there was no מעמד. It then introduces מר קשישא בריה דרב חסדא, who is about to ask רב אשי a question.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: on the first of טבת there was no מעמד, and so on. מר קשישא, the son of רב חסדא, said to רב אשי:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. It then sets up a question that מר קשישא will ask רב אשי, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that on ראש חודש טבת there was no מעמד at all. That day had three extra things: a מוסף, הלל, and the wood offering. This line only sets the stage. The actual question from מר קשישא comes right after this.
